normalization: sentence form: curly quotes -> straight, en/em dash -> hyphen, ellipsis character -> three dots, {placeholder} / {{placeholder}} / printf %s collapsed to a bare {}, whitespace collapsed to single spaces, trimmed, lowercased, trailing sentence punctuation dropped. Placeholders collapse rather than disappear, so a sentence that differs only in what its placeholder is called still matches, while a sentence with the placeholder removed does not.
keyNormalization: identifier form, for the t()-key fossil check: as above, then placeholders unwrap to their bare name, apostrophes are deleted and every other non-alphanumeric character becomes a space. Compared against a t() key leaf name with camelCase split back into words. Built only from source strings that already qualify for the sentence set, since a key can only fossilise a sentence.

entryFields.h: sha256 of the normalised string, hex

howToRegenerate: Hashes only, never strings, so this file cannot become a copy of what it screens for. Generated, not hand-edited. To rebuild: point a throwaway script at the reference UI, import normalizeSentence / normalizeIdentifier / sentenceEntry / identifierEntry / literalsInLine / jsonLeaves from string-guard.mjs (importing them is what keeps the two normalisations from drifting), harvest its locale leaves, its config string values and its bundled string literals, then write hashes plus w/c only. Never commit the harvest script or its input. Anything under minWords words is dropped: short platform labels are convergent, so matching them proves nothing.
vendorFiltered: Hashes that also match a string literal in web/node_modules were removed. The reference bundles ship third-party libraries, React among them, so a string present in a dependency this project installs is not application copy. Removing them keeps the guard from firing on ordinary library text.
